structured_output.summary: Readiness evidence is genuine and complete for the published candidate: 105 registered commands all exit 0 in one continuous 14:29–15:00 run bound to a61ee873/69eb33e, including both `--require-directional` clean extracted packages (392 s/375 s), the version-scoped `check-access-release.py --phase 28 --version 0.2.4` guard, a fresh advisory audit remediating RUSTSEC-2026-0382/0383 across both lockfiles, and honest live acceptance (1 verified, four HTTP 403). Delivery guards fail closed and readiness provably cannot advance the phase. Attempt-02's six lows are closed in source, not prose. One medium remains: the packaged README's only pointer to this release's headline feature is an absolute GitHub `v0.2.4` link that no configured step can ever create, so the immutable crates.io artifact ships a dead documentation link. Two lows persist around positionally identified consumer rows and a triplicated success marker.

findings.description: The packaged README (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:10-11 sets readme = "../../README.md" and includes README.md, while docs/ is excluded) carries the only consumer-facing pointer to this release's headline feature as an absolute link to https://github.com/cdot65/scm-sdk-rs/blob/v0.2.4/docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md. That URL cannot resolve by construction: the declared repository is Cargo.toml:9 https://git.cdot.io/cdot/scm-sdk-rs, docs/CI.md:7 states no external mirror is configured, the string appears nowhere else in the repository, and the documented delivery sequence (docs/RELEASE.md:229-240, tools/release_delivery.py:189-234) creates and verifies the annotated v0.2.4 tag only on the Forgejo remote. The link is therefore dead today and will stay dead in the immutable published archive, contradicting the receipt-conditional accuracy discipline applied in README.md:21-22,51-53,60-62, CHANGELOG.md:5-9 and docs/STABILITY.md:3-5. Prior attempts raised this and it is unchanged at this source.
findings.required_fix: Point the packaged guide link at the canonical git.cdot.io ref (or drop the absolute ref and inline the key wire-key table), or add an explicit mirror-push step plus a verified receipt to docs/RELEASE.md:229-240 and a regression in tools/test_release_024.py:28-35; then rerun both --require-directional package checks and check-access-release.py to rebind readmeSha256 in docs/checks/phase-28-release-readiness.json.

findings.description: Only the directional row is self-identifying after this phase's correction. The frozen capability probe (probe_index, lines 116-120) and the access-policy consumer (access_index = probe_index + 1, lines 132-136) share a byte-identical command ['run','--locked','--offline','--target',host] and cwd with each other and with the directional run, so their identity still rests on the producer's emission order plus packageScriptSha256/wrapperSha256 rather than on anything verifiable inside the rows themselves. This is inherited phase-23/24 design, not a regression, but it is now the weakest link in an otherwise content-addressed receipt.
findings.required_fix: Assert each external consumer's distinct stdout line, or record and verify the consumer src/main.rs digest per check row in scripts/check-package.py:191,208,221, so all three identically invoked rows are self-identifying.

findings.description: The success marker 'Directional typed models and lossless response compatibility verified offline.' is duplicated independently in three places: crates/scm-sdk/examples/directional_profiles.rs:58, this verifier constant, and the synthetic fixture at tools/test_release_024.py:245. No test binds the verifier's constant to the example's println, so editing the example's message fails qualification only after a ~390 s clean package run with the opaque error 'Directional profile consumer success output is missing or ambiguous'.
findings.required_fix: Add an assertion in tools/test_release_024.py that crates/scm-sdk/examples/directional_profiles.rs contains the verifier's marker constant read from the loaded wrapper module, so a message change fails in the cheap suite.
